what_happened: The policy took over at 4.6 s on a straight multi-lane highway. It braked hard for no clear reason, dropping from about 16 to 8 m/s, and at the same time its plan veered left out of its lane. The ego's front-left corner then hit actor 1, a car travelling alongside in the adjacent left lane. The rear contact the metrics also record happened separately from this front collision, which began first.

On a highway with a RIGHT command, the ego left the recorded path, which moves right, and drifted left across the leftmost lane onto the median edge. It went offroad at 8.2s, about 5 m from the recorded path. Before that it had braked hard behind a motorcycle (25.7 to 12.8 m/s) and was rear-ended, but the failure counted here is the drift off the road.

On a straight highway with no close lead (gap about 19–21 m and growing), the policy braked hard for no clear reason, from 17 to 8 m/s, while its plan bent left toward the adjacent lane. Actor 1 had been travelling alongside on the ego's rear-left. As the ego slowed and drifted about 1 m left of the recorded path, actor 1 pulled ahead and the ego's front clipped it. The hard braking also led to a later rear-end hit.

After handoff on a multi-lane highway, the ego braked hard for no clear reason (17 to 8 m/s, with the lead car pulling away) and its plan veered left. It moved into the adjacent left lane and its front hit actor 1, which was travelling alongside on the left. The hard braking likely also explains the later rear contact from the car behind.

On an open multi-lane highway, the policy braked hard for no visible reason (29 m/s down to 13 m/s) and was rear-ended. It then steered left, away from the human path, which kept straight and then went right as the RIGHT command asked, and went off the left edge of the road by 7.7 s. Actor 40, the following car, was overlapping the ego at that point.

After the policy took over at 4.6 s on a straight highway, it braked hard from 29 to 13 m/s with no clear reason. Some vehicle had already hit the ego's rear before 5.8 s. While the recorded human drifted right and the command switched to RIGHT, the ego kept left and steered onto the left shoulder by the guardrail, where it went off-road at 7.8 s. A vehicle (id 10) was alongside its front-right at that moment.

On a multi-lane freeway the command switched from STRAIGHT to RIGHT, and the recorded path bends right. Instead, the ego kept drifting left across the lane line at about 7 m/s. Its front struck vehicle 28, which was passing in the adjacent left lane and ended up ahead-left of the ego at impact (front collision, 4.8 m off the recorded path).

On the highway, the ego braked hard after handoff, from 20 to 11.5 m/s, even though the lead car was about 19 m ahead and moving. Its planned path then bent left, and it drifted into the side of actor 1, which was driving alongside in the left lane. The ego was also rear-ended at some point, likely because of the sudden slowdown, but the at-fault side impact with actor 1 counted as the failure.

On a multi-lane freeway the route said STRAIGHT and then RIGHT, but after handoff the ego drifted left out of its lane toward the adjacent left lane, ending up 4.7 m off the recorded path. Actor 28 was passing in that left lane, and the ego's front struck it as it cut in, still going about 7 m/s.

On a multi-lane freeway, the route command changed to RIGHT and the recorded drive moved right, but the policy steered left instead. It cut into the adjacent left lane and its front hit vehicle 28 alongside it at about 7.3 m/s, 4.8 m from where the human drove.

After handoff the ego moved left out of its lane while the recorded path stayed straight and then bore right (the command changed to RIGHT). It crossed into the neighbouring left lane and its front ran into actor 28 at about 7 m/s, 4.8 m off the recorded path.

In slow stop-and-go traffic going straight, the ego was slowing from 3.1 to 0.5 m/s behind car 24, still about 4.6 m back. It made front contact at low speed with a small orange-marked actor, probably a pedestrian or cyclist, that crossed in front of its left-front corner between the stopped cars. That actor can't be seen in the front camera in any frame, and the ego was about 2.8 m off the recorded human path.

The ego slowed to a near stop (0.1 m/s) behind a queue of cars, stopping 4.6 m behind lead car 24. It was sitting about 2.9 m off the recorded path, shifted right toward the lane line. A pedestrian or cyclist (orange in the map), threading between the queued lanes, overlapped the ego's front, which counted as a front collision while the ego was almost stationary.

The ego was creeping in slow traffic behind car 24 (the gap was still about 4.6 m when it failed), but it yawed and drifted right across the lane line, about 2.8 m from the recorded path. Its front corner hit the car queued in the right lane (likely actor 21, possibly bus 131), not the car ahead.
